overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on public participation or minutes detail, and declined to review the Mullin Rule and written-objection allegations as outside the Law. No orders issued.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission limited public participation at a February 5 virtual meeting by requiring comments through the Zoom Q&A feature.
allegations.key_passage: the chair of the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law by requiring the complainant to submit comments through the “Q&A” feature on Zoom during the February 5 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the February 5 minutes lacked sufficient detail, omitting submitted documents and inaccurately reflecting discussions and votes on the Pond Street projects.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Commission created sufficiently specific minutes of the February 5 meeting and substantially complied with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to comply with the Mullin Rule, G.L. c. 39, § 23D, on member voting after absence from a hearing session.
allegations.key_passage: Likewise, we decline to review here any allegation that the Commission violated the Mullin Rule.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to respond to written objections to the Pond Street projects before issuing orders of conditions.
allegations.key_passage: Members of the public are free to send written correspondence to a public body, but the Law does not require the public body to discuss or respond to that correspondence.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
